title: Localization certificates after quotienting by an arbitrary base ideal
statement: Let $A\to C$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $I\subseteq A$ be any ideal, and let $W\subseteq C$ be a multiplicative subset ($1\in W$, $ww'\in W$ for $w,w'\in W$). Put $B=W^{-1}C$, the ring of fractions [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], $D=C/IC$ and $R=B/IB$, where $IC$ and $IB$ are the ideals generated by the images of $I$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Write $\bar W$ for the image of $W$ in $D$. There is a ring map $\phi:D\to R$ characterized by $\phi(c\bmod IC)=(c/1\bmod IB)$. It satisfies: (a) $\phi(\bar w)$ is a unit with inverse the class of $1/w$, for every $w\in W$; (b) every element of $R$ equals $\phi(\bar c)\phi(\bar w)^{-1}$ for some $c\in C,w\in W$; (c) if $\phi(\bar c)=0$, there is $v\in W$ with $vc\in IC$, hence $\bar v\bar c=0$ in $D$. In addition the following denominator certificate holds for every finite indexed family $a_i\in I$, $d_i\in C$, $w_i\in W$ with $c/1=\sum_i a_i d_i/w_i$ in $B$: setting $w=\prod_iw_i$ and $e=\sum_i a_i d_i\prod_{j\ne i}w_j$, there is $u\in W$ with $u(wc-e)=0$, and $(uw)c=ue\in IC$. Empty sums and products are permitted. No finite generation of $I$, locality, or Noetherianity is assumed.

source.place: Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient), quotient-localization map and its inverse, with the fraction equivalence of localization applied to an extended base ideal.

proof.text: Write $f:A\to C$ and $q:B\to R$ for the given and quotient maps. By the meaning of generated ideal, for $T=C$ or $B$, $IT$ consists exactly of finite sums $\sum_i f_T(a_i)t_i$ with $a_i\in I,t_i\in T$, where $f_C=f$ and $f_B(a)=f(a)/1$. Indeed these sums form an ideal: concatenate for addition, negate the coefficients for additive inverses, and multiply the coefficients by a scalar for scalar closure; they contain every $f_T(a)$ and belong to every ideal containing these generators. This uses finitely many terms for each element, not finite generation of $I$.

source.place: Tag 00AR (section-rings-basic), generated ideals; Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient), applied to the extended ideal $IC$.

proof.text: If $x=\sum_i f(a_i)d_i\in IC$, then $x/1=\sum_i(f(a_i)/1)(d_i/1)\in IB$, so $q(x/1)=0$. Define $\phi(\bar c)=q(c/1)$. If $\bar c=\bar c\prime$, then $c-c\prime\in IC$ by the quotient kernel description, and the preceding calculation shows $q(c/1)=q(c\prime/1)$. Fraction addition and multiplication show that $c\mapsto c/1$ preserves addition, multiplication and $1$; composing with $q$ and passing to representatives proves that $\phi$ is a ring map. Every class in $D$ has a representative, which also proves the asserted characterization and uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient), proof: the map $A/I	o S^{-1}A/S^{-1}I$; Tag 00CM (section-localization), fraction operations.

proof.text: For $w\in W$, the fraction rule gives $(w/1)(1/w)=w/w=1/1$: equality of the last two fractions has witness $1\in W$ in the defining equivalence relation. Applying $q$ gives $\phi(\bar w)q(1/w)=1$, and commutativity gives the other product as $1$. Thus $\phi(\bar w)$ is a unit with inverse $q(1/w)$, proving (a).

source.place: Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient), proof: invertibility of the image of the multiplicative subset; Tag 00CM (section-localization), defining fraction relation.

proof.text: Given $r\in R$, quotient surjectivity gives $b\in B$ with $q(b)=r$, and the fraction construction gives $b=c/w$ for $c\in C,w\in W$. Since $c/w=(c/1)(1/w)$ by the multiplication formula, $r=\phi(\bar c)q(1/w)=\phi(\bar c)\phi(\bar w)^{-1}$ by step 3. This proves (b).

source.place: Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient), proof: the formula for $g$; Tag 00CM (section-localization), representatives and multiplication.

proof.text: For the finite family in the denominator assertion put $t_i=\prod_{j\ne i}w_j$ and $w=\prod_iw_i\in W$. Then $w=w_it_i$, and the fraction equivalence with witness $1$ gives $(w/1)(f(a_i)d_i/w_i)=(f(a_i)d_it_i)/1$. Multiplying the assumed relation by $w/1$ and distributing over the finite sum therefore gives $(wc)/1=e/1$, where $e=\sum_i f(a_i)d_it_i$. Hence $(wc-e)/1=0$. The zero criterion supplies $u\in W$ with $u(wc-e)=0$. Consequently $(uw)c=ue\in IC$, since $e$ is a finite sum of multiples of images of elements of $I$ and $IC$ is an ideal. For the empty family this calculation reads $w=1,e=0,c/1=0$, and the same zero criterion applies.

source.place: Tag 00CM (section-localization), fraction multiplication and the zero criterion immediately after definition-localization; expansion of Tag 00CT for an extended base ideal.

proof.text: If $\phi(\bar c)=0$, then $q(c/1)=0$, so $c/1\in IB$ by the quotient kernel description. Step 1 expresses this element as a finite sum $\sum_i(f(a_i)/1)b_i$ with $a_i\in I,b_i\in B$. Choose representatives $b_i=d_i/w_i$; the fraction multiplication rule makes the relation exactly $c/1=\sum_i f(a_i)d_i/w_i$. Step 5 gives $u,w\in W$ with $(uw)c\in IC$. Taking $v=uw\in W$ proves (c); in $D$ the product $\bar v\bar c$ is zero because its representative $vc$ lies in the quotient kernel $IC$. No cancellation or injectivity of $C\to B$ was used.

lean.statement: theorem baseIdealLocalization_certificates {A : Type u} {C : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing C] (f : A →+* C) (I : Ideal A) (W : Submonoid C) : (∃ φ : (C ⧸ I.map f) →+* (Localization W ⧸ I.map ((algebraMap C (Localization W)).comp f)), (∀ c : C, φ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map f) c) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map ((algebraMap C (Localization W)).comp f)) (Localization.mk c (1 : W))) ∧ (∀ ψ : (C ⧸ I.map f) →+* (Localization W ⧸ I.map ((algebraMap C (Localization W)).comp f)), (∀ c : C, ψ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map f) c) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map ((algebraMap C (Localization W)).comp f)) (Localization.mk c (1 : W))) → ψ = φ) ∧ (∀ w : W, IsUnit (φ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map f) (w : C))) ∧ φ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map f) (w : C)) * Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map ((algebraMap C (Localization W)).comp f)) (Localization.mk 1 w) = 1) ∧ (∀ r : Localization W ⧸ I.map ((algebraMap C (Localization W)).comp f), ∃ (c : C) (w : W), r = φ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map f) c) * Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map ((algebraMap C (Localization W)).comp f)) (Localization.mk 1 w)) ∧ (∀ c : C, φ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map f) c) = 0 → ∃ v : W, (v : C) * c ∈ I.map f ∧ Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map f) (v : C) * Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map f) c = 0)) ∧ (∀ (ι : Type t) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (a : ι → I) (d : ι → C) (w : ι → W) (c : C) (p : W) (e : C), p = ∏ i, w i → e = ∑ i, f (a i) * d i * ∏ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, (w j : C) → (Localization.mk c (1 : W) : Localization W) = ∑ i, Localization.mk (f (a i) * d i) (w i) → ∃ u : W, (u : C) * ((p : C) * c - e) = 0 ∧ ((u * p : W) : C) * c = (u : C) * e ∧ (u : C) * e ∈ I.map f)
